clues.text: In this modern-day country, the 722 Battle of Covadonga sparked a centuries-long war against Islamic forces.
One king of this country imprisoned his mother, Joanna the Mad, and sponsored Magellan’s circumnavigation of the globe.
clues.source: 2020 TAILS, Packet TAILS Replacements and Tiebreakers

clues.text: The Ebro (AY-bro) Valley is in this nation that owns the Balearic (BAH-lee-AH-rick) Islands and the Canary Islands.
During the reign of Philip II, poor winds foiled this country’s attempted invasion of England using a namesake “Armada” of ships.
The Alhambra Decree expelled practicing Jews from this country, which was unofficially unified after the marriage of monarchs from Castile and Aragon.
This country was blamed for a shipwreck near Havana Harbor that destroyed the USS Maine.
This country was once ruled by dictator Francisco Franco.
Because its King Alfonso XIII became ill during it, the 1918 Influenza Pandemic was named after what Iberian nation, ruled from Madrid?
The Iberian Peninsula is shared by Portugal and what nation whose capital is Madrid?
Name this Iberian country long led by Francisco Franco.
This onetime lawyer-in-training claimed that a spontaneous prayer to St. Anne during a storm led him to become a monk.
This man joined one profession after barely missing a lightning strike and exclaiming to Saint Anne, and this friend of Philipp Melanchthon became enraged by the actions of Johann Tetzel.
This man at times opposed the Cardinal Cajetan, Andreas Karlstadt, and Thomas Muntzer, the last of whom he criticized for leading the excessively violent Peasant's War.
This man was called a “wild boar from the forest” in a text that asks one figure to “ judge your own cause.”
Along with Ulrich Zwingli, this man attended the Marburg Colloquy.
He urged nobles to “smite, slay, and stab” the title group in his work “Against the Murderous, Thieving Hordes of Peasants.”
Angered by the actions of Johann Tetzel, he was excommunicated by Leo X at the Diet of Worms after writing a document prompted by the sale of “sin-erasing” indulgences.
The Edict of Worms excommunicated this man for his failure to recant his writings, which were famously nailed to the doors of the Wittenberg chapel.
This man espoused justification by faith alone in a work he nailed to a church door, the 95 Theses.
Name this German friar who initiated the Protestant Reformation when he composed his 95 Theses in 1515.

answerlines: Cossacks [accept Don Cossacks or Zaporizhzhian Cossacks; accept Kazak even though that’s similar to the unrelated “Kazakh”; prompt on Russians or Ukranians or Russian cavalry or Russian soldiers]

clues.text: A disastrous land invasion of British India by these people was averted by the Pahlen Plot.
Leaders of these people carried the ceremonial bulava mace.
Leaders of these people would have received titles in the Treaty of Hadiach (“HAH-dyach”).
Astrakhan was pillaged and then transformed into a republic by a leader of this group, Stenka Razin.
The Khanate of Sibir was overthrown by one of these people, Yermak.
Besides Stenka Razin and Mazepa, one of them became convinced that he was Peter the Great and rebelled against Catherine the Great.
The Zaporozhian hetman of these people, Ivan Mazepa, defected to Sweden during the Great Northern War.
Yemelyan Pugachev led these people in an uprising that was put down by Catherine the Great.
Name these nomadic, militaristic people that largely lived along the Don and Dnieper (“NEE-per”) Rivers in Ukraine and Russia.
What semi-nomadic horsemen lived on the steppes of the Russian Empire?
